#/items/oneOf/0/properties/word.rationale: Uppercasing is mechanical, so any case is accepted. Other letters (umlauts, accents) are rejected: transliteration varied by operator and era, so the caller decides it.

#/items/oneOf/1/properties/name.rationale: Enigma operators wrote foreign names twice between Xs, because a garbled name cannot be guessed from context.

#/items/oneOf/2/properties/number.rationale: No machine had digit keys. Numbers are a string so leading zeros (0600) survive.

#/items/oneOf/3/properties/punct.rationale: Which marks an operator can write is in each operator's spec. Leaving a mark out is the operator's judgment: omit the token.

#/items/oneOf/4/properties/gap.rationale: Separators are never inserted implicitly. The M-209 1947 manual made spacing a per-message random choice against cribs, so the choice has to be an input to stay reproducible.
